types.name: app.Config
types.doc: Per-app settings the hosts read at compile time.

fields.name: timer_armed
fields.doc: Whether the timer runs from startup; `cx.set_timer` starts and stops it later.

fields.name: draw
fields.doc: The app's draw types and their pool capacities; a type's id is its index.

fields.name: batch_cap
fields.doc: Upper bound on batches per frame: distinct (layer, type, texture) runs.

fields.name: batch_order
fields.doc: How a layer's batches order: by first appearance, or by `draw`'s order, then texture (`draw/pools.zig`, section 1).

fields.name: area_cap
fields.doc: Upper bound on hit areas per frame; the rest are counted and not hittable.

fields.name: point_cap
fields.doc: Upper bound on path points per frame, when a registered type reads points.

fields.name: theme
fields.doc: The scheme the app starts with (`theme.zig`); `cx.set_theme` switches it at run time.

fields.name: decorations
fields.doc: Who should draw the window's frame natively (section 4c): `server` asks the window manager; `client` means the app draws it (`widgets.WindowButtons`).

types.name: app.Declaration
types.doc: One declaration of the contract: its name, the type `check` requires, and when.

types.name: app.Need
types.doc: When a declaration of the contract must be present (section 2).

tags.name: optional
tags.doc: An app may declare it on its own.

types.name: bench.At
types.doc: A point at `(x, y)` logical pixels from the target's top-left.

types.name: bench.Drag
types.doc: A left drag: press at `(from_x, from_y)` from the target's top-left, move by `(dx, dy)`, release.

types.name: bench.DropFiles
types.doc: Files dropped at the target's centre (section 2b).

types.name: bench.File
types.doc: A file a `drop` step carries: its name and its bytes as parts.

fields.name: readable
fields.doc: False lists it as a folder would be: unreadable, size 0.

types.name: bench.Finger
types.doc: One finger's part of a `touch` step: what it does at `(x, y)`, absolute logical pixels.

types.name: bench.Part
types.doc: Bytes repeated `repeat` times: a piece of a dropped file (section 2b).

types.name: bench.Press
types.doc: A key pressed and released; `text` is what it types, at most `input.key_text_cap` bytes, and nothing by default (a key that types nothing: `.{ .key = .{ .key = .end } }`).

types.name: bench.Scenario
types.doc: A scripted run: steps once, steps repeated, and the frames to measure (module guide).

fields.name: cycle
fields.doc: Repeated while measuring; empty when the app presents frames by itself.

fields.name: regress
fields.doc: `--regress` renders it and compares its last frame with the golden file (`host/headless.zig`).

types.name: bench.Target
types.doc: An area of the last frame, by id, with the name and index it came from for messages.

types.name: bench.Turn
types.doc: A wheel turn at the target's centre.

constants.name: app.timer_period_ms_max
constants.doc: Upper bound for `Config.timer_period_ms`, chosen so a period given in the wrong unit is rejected at build time.

constants.name: app.area_cap_max
constants.doc: Largest `Config.area_cap`, the hit areas one frame records (`ui/areas.zig`).

constants.name: app.point_cap_max
constants.doc: Largest `Config.point_cap`, the path points one frame holds (`draw/pools.zig`).

constants.name: app.regress_side_max
constants.doc: Largest side of `App.regress_size`, in logical pixels.

constants.name: app.render_side_max
constants.doc: Largest side of `App.render_size_max`, in device pixels: the largest target.

functions.name: app.Context
functions.doc: The UI context type `App.event`, `App.timer`, and `App.draw` receive, built from `App.config`.

functions.name: app.start
functions.doc: Records `App.config`'s timer (section 4), its theme (section 4b), and its batch order in a freshly initialized context.

functions.name: app.has_args
functions.doc: Whether `App` takes the host's leftover arguments (section 4d).

functions.name: app.start_timer
functions.doc: The step 30 name of `start`, which it now is.

functions.name: app.has_producer
functions.doc: Whether `App` declares a producer on another thread (section 4e).

functions.name: app.has_produce
functions.doc: Whether the app steps its producer by frame where no thread runs it (section 4e).

functions.name: app.declarations
functions.doc: The contract's declarations for `App`, the table `conformance` checks against: the one place their types are written.

functions.name: app.conformance
functions.doc: Returns null when `App` satisfies the contract, otherwise a message naming the first problem.

functions.name: app.check
functions.doc: Fails the build with a message naming the missing or mistyped declaration.

scenario_steps.name: click
scenario_steps.doc: A left click at the target's centre, then the pointer leaves the window.

scenario_steps.name: right_click
scenario_steps.doc: A right click at the point, then the pointer leaves the window.

scenario_steps.name: hover
scenario_steps.doc: The pointer moves to the point and stays there: no leave, so the target stays hovered.

scenario_steps.name: drag
scenario_steps.doc: Move to the start, press, move by the delta, release; the pointer rests at the end.

scenario_steps.name: hold
scenario_steps.doc: Move to the start, press, move by the delta, and move there again; no release, so the press stays held and a drag between widgets stays in flight for the dump.

scenario_steps.name: release
scenario_steps.doc: Move to the point and release the left button there: ends a `hold` a frame later, so what the hold's frame drew (a dock's edge strips) takes the drop.

scenario_steps.name: drop_hover
scenario_steps.doc: A file drag moves over the target's centre and stays (section 2b).

scenario_steps.name: drop
scenario_steps.doc: Files dragged to the target's centre and dropped; accepted ones are delivered.

scenario_steps.name: touch
scenario_steps.doc: Every listed finger does its part in one frame, in order, so a chord lands in one frame (module guide, section 2d).
